ORGANATIONAL CONTEXT
The Institute of Business Studies (IBS), from its humble beginning in 1987 as an arm of Nades &  Associates, primarily providing revision classes for the needs of Papua New Guinea Institute of Accountants (now CPA PNG), has evolved into a private university-level Institution over the last thirty-four years. It was elevated as a University in January 2017 and offers its own degree programmes in the fields of Accounting & Finance, Business & Management, Economics & Development Studies, and Information Technology.
Today, we are one of the largest business schools in the country and continue to grow into the future. These successes are the fruits of our dedicated team members’ commitment to making a difference in Papua New Guinea through their efforts in helping educate fellow citizens.
The University has been affiliated with the Southern Cross University (SCU) of Australia since 1999 and offers its degree programmes in Accounting, Business, and Information Technology. The affiliation with Southern Cross University has made IBS the first and only Institution to offer internationally recognised Bachelor programmes face-to-face in Papua New Guinea
We strive to be the pioneer institution for business education in PNG. Some of our accomplishments to date are listed below:
Only educational Institution to operate a Career Centre.
Only the organisation has a “Centre of Excellence” for Leadership & Management Development.
Only private University established as per the decision of NEC and Gazettal.
Only private Institution to hold the status of “Study Centre – for the University of Papua New Guinea.” Till 2016, for 22 years.
Examination Centre for the majority of Australian & NZ Universities.
Test Centre for ICDL, CISCO, Pearson VUE & Prometric.
Established partnerships with Oracle Academy, Red Hat Academy, and the All-India Management Association (AIMA), among others.
To bridge the gap between academia and industry, facilitated Memoranda of Understanding with organisations such as BSP, Telikom, CPL, Vodafone, Women’s Micro Bank, Theodist, Barlow Industries, and CEFI.
First, publish bi-annual Journal of Business & Research in Papua New Guinea.
Accredited professional bodies in PNG & Australia and ISO 9001:2015 certified University.
As a private tertiary institution, our survival and growth depend heavily on high-quality teaching, learning, and impactful research that strengthens our reputation and attracts students and partners. The role of the Head of Research needs to be modern, innovative, and strategically positioned.
Job Summary:
The Secretary will assist the Council and the Vice Chancellor by managing official communications, preparing documents, and organizing meetings. The ideal candidate must be a qualified lawyer with at least one year of legal practice experience. The role requires strong organizational skills, professional handling of legal and administrative tasks, and the ability to support high-level university governance.
Key Responsibilities:
Prepare agendas and organize meetings for the Council and the Vice Chancellor.
Take minutes and keep records of meetings.
Handle official correspondence and document filing.
Provide legal advice when needed, based on your legal background.
Assist in drafting and reviewing legal and administrative documents.
Ensure timely follow-up on action points from meetings.
Maintain confidentiality of sensitive information.
Support the Vice Chancellor and Council members with administrative tasks.
Requirements:
Qualification: Bachelor's degree in Law or related field (LL.B.) with at least one year of legal practice.
Good knowledge of legal procedures and documentation.
Strong organizational and communication skills.
Ability to handle confidential information professionally.
Responsible, reliable, and detail-oriented.
Working Hours:
Full-time, Monday to Friday, with occasional extra hours for meetings or urgent tasks.
Who Can Apply:
Qualified lawyers with at least one year of legal practice and administrative experience, preferably with experience supporting executive or academic bodies in a university setting.

A CAREER WITH US:
At IBS we believe that everyone has been gifted with natural talents and learnt skills. Our recruitment process is designed to help candidates understand this and enable us to better match you with a role that you will not only be able to do but enjoy doing. Career progression is also important to us and believes that each employee should be at the driving seat of their career progression - this means your manager will discuss with you where you want to be in the future and be more of a coach for you in terms of giving you feedback on areas you need to work on to be your best and achieve your goals. 26047.description:
About Newmont
At Newmont, we’re not just a world-leading gold and metals producer – we’re a team united by our commitment to shaping a more inclusive, sustainable, and responsible mining industry. Joining us means becoming part of a global, diverse workforce where everyone is valued, empowered, and encouraged to grow. Our people are the heart of our success, bringing exceptional skill, integrity, and dedication to everything we do as an organization and we’re dedicated to creating a workplace where everyone can thrive.
About Lihir
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Your Impact
As a Metallurgist at Newmont, you will be instrumental in optimising metallurgical performance, supporting safe and efficient processing operations, and ensuring we maximise value from every tonne processed. Your work will directly influence gold recovery, plant stability, and continual improvement across our processing systems.
As part of our team, you will
Provide technical support and troubleshooting for metallurgical and processing site operations.
Collaborate with geology, mining, maintenance, plant operations and other key operational teams to resolve operational challenges.
Contribute to process improvement initiatives and the deployment of new technologies.
Deliver accurate metallurgical analysis, reporting, plant surveys, testwork programs and plant equipment inspections.
Coach, mentor, and support colleagues and graduate metallurgists to build team capability.
Uphold Newmont’s safety values through visible leadership, Critical Control Verifications, and proactive risk management.
Identify cost‑reduction opportunities and minimise waste within the processing value chain.
Ensure compliance with the PNG Mine Safety Act, Newmont Safety Systems, Environmental policies, and departmental procedures.
Prerequisites for your success in this role
Bachelor’s degree in Metallurgy, Mineral Processing, Chemical Engineering, or similar.

26087.description:
About Lihir
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Purpose
The
Technician, Condition Monitoring
will conduct condition monitoring and diagnostic activities to assess the health and performance of equipment, ensuring early detection of potential failures and supporting proactive maintenance to improve asset reliability and operational efficiency.
Essential Duties
Execute condition monitoring and diagnostic activities.
Assess collected data to detect anomalies and provide corrective actions.
Liaise with maintenance teams to ensure timely intervention and resolution of identified issues.
Maintain and administer condition monitoring tools and equipment to ensure data accuracy.
Prepare and report findings from condition monitoring activities for use in maintenance planning.
Execute inspections of critical equipment to evaluate operating conditions and potential risks.
Assist root cause analysis (RCA) processes to address equipment failures.
Deliver training to operational and maintenance staff on condition monitoring practices.
Monitor compliance with safety and operational standards during monitoring activities and report any non-conformance to Supervisor.
Support continuous improvement initiatives to enhance the effectiveness of condition monitoring programs.
Training & Experience
Trade qualified and/or holding a higher certification or degree in Mechanical or Electrical Engineering (or equivalent).
Proven experience in vibration data collection and analysis within heavy industry, preferably in a fixed plant environment.
Strong knowledge of complex rotating equipment, including maintenance strategies and fault diagnostics.
Demonstrated problem-solving capability with a strong aptitude for resolving technical challenges.
Well-developed computer skills, including the Microsoft Office Suite and Power BI.
Experience using SAP or similar Computerised Maintenance Management Systems (CMMS).
Working knowledge of vibration analysis software is desirable.
Solid understanding of condition monitoring techniques, including vibration analysis, thermography, oil sampling and analysis interpretation, and non-destructive testing (e.g. ultrasonic thickness testing, dye penetrant testing, magnetic particle inspection, laser alignment).
Class 6 PNG Driver’s Licence preferred but not essential.
Working Conditions
This is a FIFO role on a 21:21 roster.
If you feel that you could make a meaningful contribution in this role, we encourage you to discuss this opportunity with your current people leader and how it aligns with your longer term career goals.
To support you in your application, we have created a range of resources available to all Newmont People including information on eligibility criteria and FAQs. Find out more by visiting our page in Discovery: Internal Employee Resources
As a current employee or contractor, please submit your application is MS Word or Adobe format online via the Internal Job Postings link on Discovery.
If you have issues applying through Discovery or would like to learn more about the role before applying, please contact the relevant member of our Talent Acquisition Team.
Apply

Join a passionate team dedicated to a stronger, more vibrant capital.
Grow Your Career in a dynamic urban environment
Build a Legacy: Lead transformative projects shaping the future of Port Moresby
NC Salary Grade: NC 12
Location:
Tarpot, 4 Mile, Port Moresby, NCD
Reporting to:
Manager - City Works
About the National Capital District Commission (NCDC)
The National Capital District Commission (NCDC) is the statutory authority responsible for governing and managing Papua New Guinea’s capital city, Port Moresby.
Unlike other parts of PNG that fall under provincial administrations, Port Moresby sits within a unique administrative area – the National Capital District (NCD) established under its own Act of Parliament. The NCDC is mandated to plan, manage, regulate and shape the capital city on behalf of its residents, communities, and the nation as a whole.
As the gateway to Papua New Guinea, Port Moresby plays a critical national role. The NCDC’s responsibilities extend beyond routine municipal services to include city-wide planning, regulation, infrastructure coordination, social development, and institutional reform in a rapidly growing and complex urban environment.
About the Role
The
Electrical Engineer – Road Asset Maintenance
is a specialized technical leadership position within the National Capital District Commission (NCDC) under the Engineering & Infrastructure Directorate, classified as
NC.12
. Based at
Tarpot, 4 Mile
, the role reports directly to the
Manager – City Works
and involves the supervision of both internal subordinates and external contractors. This position requires extensive expertise—typically 7 to 10 years of experience—in civil engineering and project management to effectively monitor and evaluate the maintenance and construction of road-related infrastructure. Key responsibilities include executing detailed maintenance plans, coordinating emergency responses for electrical failures, and leading improvement projects designed to enhance the reliability of the city’s electrical assets.
Role Purpose
The primary purpose of this role is to oversee the
maintenance, operational functionality, and performance
of critical road assets throughout the NCDC to ensure public safety and urban efficiency. The Electrical Engineer is specifically responsible for the upkeep and reliability of
traffic lights, streetlights, and street furniture
, ensuring all systems adhere to road regulatory standards. By facilitating seamless coordination between internal technical teams and external contractors, the role aims to minimize infrastructure downtime and implement strategic upgrades. Ultimately, the position exists to maintain a safe and well-lit transit environment for the residents of Port Moresby, contributing directly to the Commission’s vision for a modernized city.
Key Responsibilities
Project Management & Operational Reliability: Ensure and maintain the continuous and safe operation of traffic lights, streetlights, and street furniture (including bus stops, signage, traffic signs, bins and bollards, sculptures), ensuring these critical road assets are functional, well-maintained, and compliant with all relevant standards and regulations.
Lead and Coordinate Maintenance Activities: Oversee and coordinate both internal teams and external contractors in the planning, budgeting, scheduling and execution of maintenance and repair projects, ensuring timely and cost-effective delivery while adhering to quality and safety standards.
Innovation and Continuous Improvement: Identify and implement opportunities for technological advancements and process improvements in road asset management, enhancing efficiency, improving reliability, reducing costs, and improving service delivery to the NCD community.
Education & Qualifications
Minimum: Trade Certificate in Electrical Engineering also highly desired.
Preferred: Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, or related field.
Minimum: Must have Driver’s License (minimum Class 3)
Preferred: Membership with the Institution of Engineers PNG highly desirable
Must have Grade 12 Certificate
Skills & Knowledge
Technical Expertise in Road Asset Management: In-depth knowledge of the maintenance, repair, and operation of road assets, including traffic lights, streetlights, and street furniture, to ensure they are managed efficiently and effectively.
Project and Contractor Management: Strong knowledge of project management principles, including planning, budgeting, and scheduling, as well as experience in managing contractors to ensure they adhere to contracts and deliver high-quality work.
Risk Management and Contingency Planning: Expertise in identifying potential risks associated with road asset maintenance, as well as developing and implementing contingency plans to mitigate disruptions and emergencies.
Stakeholder Engagement and Communication: Proficient in collaborating with various internal and external stakeholders, including government agencies, contractors, and the public, to align maintenance activities and ensure effective communication and coordination.
Regulatory and Compliance Standards: Comprehensive knowledge of regulations relevant to road asset needs and maintenance; including Physical Planning Act (1989), Land Act (1996), Road Traffic Act (2014), National Water and Sewerage Act (1986), National Water Supply and Sanitation Act (2016), Road (Management & Fund) Act 2020, National Roads Authority Act (2003), National Capital District Commission Act (2001)
Proficient knowledge in project management software, CAD software and Microsoft Office Suite.
Strong project management skills, with a track record of successfully delivering projects on time and within budget and very critical with attention to detail.
Self-driven, disciplined, organised and motivated, able to work with minimal supervision to deliver quality strategic outcomes in a demanding and high-pressure environment.
Strong leadership, communication, interpersonal and conflict resolution skills to coordinate contractors and staff with fairness, sensitivity, tact, discretion and confidence.
A drive for continuous improvement towards new effective and efficient processes.
Experience in the preparation of detailed and accurate design plans and technical reports.
Ability to maintain confidentiality and demonstrate high levels of ethical conduct and honesty.
Must be dedicated to the advancement of NCDC, its goals and vision for Port Moresby.
Work Experience
At least 7 – 10 years of experience in Civil Engineering and project management roles, particularly in areas of road asset maintenance and/or construction
At least 3-5 years in a leadership role supervising contractors & staff.
3-5 years of contractor and project management and monitoring and evaluation of contractors.
Why Join NCDC?
This role offers a unique opportunity to influence how data shapes the future of Papua New Guinea’s capital city. You will work at the centre of urban development, infrastructure planning, and service delivery—contributing to projects that leave a lasting legacy for Port Moresby.
Ready to Make an Impact?
If you are passionate about data-driven decision-making and city transformation, we encourage you to apply.
How to Apply
Interested candidates are encouraged to:
Review the available roles and position requirements
Prepare to upload relevant supporting documentation
Cover Letter
Up-to-date CV, include in the one file along with your CV: copies of educational qualifications and a copy of a valid driver's licence (if applicable)
Click on the "APPLY NOW" button and submit an application through the Peopleconnexion PNG application portal.
Open to Port Moresby residents only.
Due to volume of candidates, only short-listed candidates will be contacted regarding applicant progress.
Applications are assessed on merit, capability, and alignment with NCDC’s values and service mandate.
Be part of the team shaping the future of Port Moresby — apply today.
Apply

The primary purpose of this role is to plan, coordinate, and deliver community engagement initiatives specifically designed to reduce the prevalence of gender-based violence (GBV) in Port Moresby. Knowledge of program design, implementation, and evaluation processes, particularly in prevention and awareness initiatives.

Strong communication and interpersonal skills to coordinate a team of employees with fairness, sensitivity, tact, discretion and confidence.

Excellent stakeholder engagement and relationship-building skills.

Proficient in designing and delivering quality outcomes based on research, evidence-based programs and cultural sensitivity.

The National Capital District Commission (NCDC) is the statutory authority responsible for governing and managing Papua New Guinea’s capital city, Port Moresby.
Unlike other parts of PNG that fall under provincial administrations, Port Moresby sits within a unique administrative area – the National Capital District (NCD) established under its own Act of Parliament. About the Role
The
Urban Planner (Environment and Risk Management)
is a specialist planning role responsible for integrating environmental sustainability, climate resilience, and hazard risk reduction into urban planning and development processes across the National Capital District. The role supports the preparation and implementation of urban plans, zoning frameworks, and development assessments that respond to environmental challenges such as flooding, landslides, coastal erosion, and settlement growth in high-risk areas. Working closely with planning colleagues, engineers, environmental authorities, and community stakeholders, the role contributes to coordinated and risk-informed urban development outcomes.
Role Purpose
The primary purpose of the Urban Planner (Environment and Risk Management) is to support evidence-based urban planning that promotes environmental responsibility, climate adaptation, and disaster risk reduction. The role ensures environmental and hazard considerations—such as green space protection, drainage and waste planning, ecological integrity, and resilience strategies—are incorporated into planning policies, land use decisions, and infrastructure planning. Through technical analysis, stakeholder collaboration, and policy support, the role contributes to building a safer, more resilient, and sustainable Port Moresby aligned with NCDC’s long-term development vision.
Key Responsibilities
Integrate environmental sustainability, climate resilience, and disaster risk reduction into urban plans, zoning frameworks, and development assessments to support safe, compliant, and sustainable growth across the National Capital District.
Provide technical planning input on environmental and hazard risks through development reviews, spatial analysis, GIS mapping, and preparation of reports and submissions for Planning Board and internal decision-making processes.
Collaborate with internal branches, government agencies, and technical partners to support risk-informed planning outcomes, maintain environmental planning data, and assist with consultant coordination and procurement activities in line with NCDC policies and procedures.
Education & Qualifications
Minimum: Diploma in Urban and Regional Planning, Environmental Management, Physical Planning, Geography, or a related field, combined with relevant training in environmental risk assessment, GIS, or urban resilience.
Preferred: Bachelor in Urban and Regional Planning, Environmental Science, Environmental Planning, Geography, or a closely related field from a recognised institution..
Preferred: Eligible for membership with a recognised planning or community development body (e.g., PNG Institute of Planners or similar professional organisation)
Skills & Knowledge
Knowledge of relevant legislation, or willingness to acquire knowledge of: Physical Planning Act (1989 & 2001), Physical Planning Regulation (2007), Land Act (1996), NCDC Act (2001), Environmental Act (2000) and Public Procurement Act (2021).
Understanding of environmental risks and hazard-prone areas common in Port Moresby, including flood zones, erosion-prone slopes, and informal settlement vulnerabilities.
Knowledge of climate adaptation strategies, sustainable land use, and green infrastructure approaches in urban contexts.
Familiarity with planning tools that integrate risk mitigation and environmental sustainability into development controls and zoning.
Understanding of how environmental planning interacts with infrastructure provision, land use policy, and urban resilience.
Environmental and Urban Planning Practice: Practice: Demonstrated ability to contribute to planning processes that integrate environmental risk and sustainability principles.
Risk Analysis and Mapping:Skilled in analysing hazard data and applying findings to planning proposals and zoning recommendations.
Communication and Stakeholder Engagement: Strong ability to engage technical agencies, planning consultants, and community stakeholders on environmental issues.
Regulatory Interpretation: Ability to interpret and apply environmental planning instruments, zoning schemes, and disaster risk reduction policies.
Technical Proficiency: Competent in GIS, environmental mapping tools, and Microsoft Office Suite.
Professionalism and Public Sector Values: Demonstrated integrity, discretion, and commitment to ethical standards and community service.
Work Experience
Minimum of 3 years’ experience in urban, environmental, or land use planning, with exposure to environmental risk management in a public or municipal setting.
Experience contributing to development plans, hazard risk assessments, and land use policies that incorporate environmental and climate considerations.
Prior involvement in projects related to disaster risk reduction, green infrastructure, or environmentally sensitive areas is desirable.
Experience working with multidisciplinary teams, government agencies, and planning consultants in an urban development context is an advantage.

About the Role
The Mapping Officer role combines office-based GIS and mapping work with regular field visits to settlements and upgrading project sites. The position involves preparing and updating maps, managing spatial data, and supporting settlement planning activities in coordination with the Settlement Development Planner and Lands Officer. The role also includes GPS data collection and on-site verification to confirm physical conditions and ensure mapping accuracy.
Role Purpose
The purpose of the role is to provide accurate, reliable, and up-to-date spatial information to support settlement planning, community consultation, and the delivery of upgrading projects. By working closely with the City Data Branch (GIS Unit) and project stakeholders, the Mapping Officer ensures mapping standards are maintained and spatial data effectively supports safe, feasible, and well-coordinated development outcomes.
Key Responsibilities
Prepare and maintain accurate settlement maps, subdivision layouts, and spatial datasets to support planning, design, community consultation, and delivery of the Settlements to Suburbs Program.
Conduct GPS-based field data collection and on-site verification to confirm physical conditions and ensure spatial accuracy and reliability.
Update and manage spatial data using approved GIS systems, ensuring consistency with NCDC mapping standards and City Data Branch requirements.
Work closely with the Settlement Development Planner, Lands Officer, and Project Coordinators to ensure spatial information supports safe, feasible, and well-coordinated upgrading works.
Collaborate with the City Data Branch (GIS Unit) to access base datasets, align mapping outputs with enterprise standards, and obtain technical support when required.
Prepare clear, accessible maps and visual materials for community awareness, consultation, and stakeholder engagement activities.
Support community engagement by presenting mapped information in a clear and culturally respectful manner.
Maintain organised digital records of spatial data, field notes, and map updates in accordance with NCDC procedures.

Preferred:
Minimum: Diploma in Geographical Information Systems (GIS), Cartography, Surveying, Geography, or a related technical discipline.
Preferred:
Bachelor’s Degree in GIS, Surveying, Urban Planning, or Geomatics. Certification in GIS software (e.g., ArcGIS, QGIS) is highly regarded.
Skills & Knowledge
Proficiency using GIS and mapping software (e.g., ArcGIS, QGIS, AutoCAD Map or similar).
Competent in GPS/GNSS data capture, processing, and field verification techniques.
Ability to present spatial information clearly for both technical and community audiences.
Strong verbal and written communication skills to support coordination and engagement.
Effective organisational and time management skills to manage multiple site-based tasks.
Ability to work both independently and collaboratively with multidisciplinary teams, including the Planner, Lands Officer, Project Coordinators, and City Data GIS Unit.
High attention to detail and commitment to spatial accuracy and data integrity.
Commitment to NCDC values of professionalism, accountability, cultural respect, and service delivery.
Work Experience
Minimum of three (3) years’ experience in GIS, surveying, or spatial data work, preferably related to urban development or settlement upgrading.
Demonstrated experience in producing maps and spatial datasets used for planning, design, or project coordination.
Field experience in data collection and verification, including work in informal or community-based settings, and coordination with government agencies or contractors is an advantage.

About the Role
The
Legal Officer
is a specialist position within the Family & GEWE (Gender Equity and Women Empowerment) Branch of the Community & Social Development Division. Based at NCDC City Hall in Waigani, this role operates at the intersection of legal advocacy, network building, and policy formulation. The position involves high-level stakeholder engagement, including representing clients in court and managing partnerships with legal firms, pro bono practitioners, and universities. Dealing with sensitive cases involving abuse, neglect, and gender-based violence (GBV), the role requires a professional with deep resilience, ethical conduct, and a strong commitment to human rights.
Role Purpose
Reporting to the Manager – Family, Welfare & GBV Services, the primary purpose of this role is to facilitate access to justice for women, children, and marginalized groups in Port Moresby. The Officer is responsible for developing a robust network of legal professionals to provide pro bono aid to vulnerable clients while simultaneously creating capacity-building opportunities for legal students. The NCDC is mandated to plan, manage, regulate and shape the capital city on behalf of its residents, communities, and the nation as a whole.
As the gateway to Papua New Guinea, Port Moresby plays a critical national role. The NCDC’s responsibilities extend beyond routine municipal services to include city-wide planning, regulation, infrastructure coordination, social development, and institutional reform in a rapidly growing and complex urban environment.
About the Role
The
Building Inspector (Class II-IX)
is a technical regulatory position within the Building Authority Branch of the Regulatory Services Directorate. Based at NCDC City Hall in Waigani, the role requires a significant presence in the field to conduct physical inspections of various building types, including multi-unit residential buildings (Class II), hostels, hotels, schools, and commercial or industrial facilities (Class III-IX). The position operates under the guidance of the Senior Building Inspector and involves regular interaction with developers, contractors, and other professionals such as engineers and architects. Because the role involves enforcing compliance and identifying illegal or unsafe structures, it requires a high degree of professional integrity, firmness, and the ability to work under pressure.
Role Purpose
The primary purpose of this role is to ensure that all Class II through IX buildings within the National Capital District are constructed in strict accordance with the PNG National Building Code, Fire Safety standards, and the original plans approved by the Building Board. By monitoring construction sites, identifying non-compliant works, and verifying that buildings are structurally sound, the Building Inspector plays a critical role in protecting public safety and maintaining the architectural integrity of the city’s urban environment. This oversight ensures that both new developments and alterations meet the statutory requirements necessary for a safe and functional capital city.
Key Responsibilities
Inspections & Investigations – performs Class II-IX building inspections and investigations to monitor and ensure they meet safety and structural laws and guidelines, and that buildings are accurately built to original plans submitted to NCDC.
Reporting – Provide detailed reports on building inspections detailing defects and non-compliance aspects to be rectified to the Senior Building Inspector – Class II-IX for their attention and action.
Communication – Communicate activities, inspections, timelines and reporting requirements to your supervisor in a timely matter to ensure efficient progress with building developments.
Education & Qualifications
Bachelor’s degree in Building and Construction Management or Civil Engineering from a reputable university.
Professional membership to at least one of the professional institutes including PNG Institute of Builders, PNG Institute of Architect or PNG Institute of Engineers
PNG Driver’s license (min. class 3)
Skills & Knowledge
Knowledge of the principles of building and construction and the building development and physical planning process.
Knowledge of CAD drawing and accurate interpretation of technical drawings.
Knowledge of relevant legislations, regulations, Acts, and standards including, but not limited to: Building Act Chapter 301 1971 and Regulations 1994; Public Health Act and Regulations; Physical Planning Act 1989 and Regulations 2007; Land Act 1996; Environment Act 2002; National Capital District Act 2001 and Public Finance Act.
Knowledge of PNG Construction Standards and Building Materials
Strong communication, problem-solving and interpersonal skills displaying a sense of fairness, sensitivity, tact, discretion, and confidence.
A drive for continuous improvement towards new effective and efficient processes.
Strong computer and writing skills to produce quality reports.
Ability to interpret CAD drawings and building plans.
Ability to work with minimal supervision, meet demands and deadlines, work under high pressure, maintain confidentiality, be organized, self-disciplined, self-motivated, honest and reliable.
Must be dedicated to the advancement of NCDC, its goals and vision for Port Moresby.
Exposure to, and skills to oversee the assessment of development proposals for complex, prominent or sensitive projects.
Experience in decision making and providing advice to assist others in making decisions, and to work collaboratively with professionals from various disciplines as part of a team.
Ability to consider and balance competing issues and arrive at a pragmatic outcome.
Work Experience
At least five (5) years of Industrial and or building construction experience at a Senior Level, or if not, to have held an Officer level role for at least 5 years in NCD with the necessary educational requirements, or to have sat in an equivalent Inspector level role for the last 2 years.
At least five (5) years’ experience in using and interpreting CAD designs.
Why Join NCDC?
This role offers a unique opportunity to influence how data shapes the future of Papua New Guinea’s capital city. You will work at the centre of urban development, infrastructure planning, and service delivery—contributing to projects that leave a lasting legacy for Port Moresby.
Ready to Make an Impact?
If you are passionate about data-driven decision-making and city transformation, we encourage you to apply.
How to Apply

Review the available roles and position requirements

Click on the "APPLY NOW" button and submit an application through the Peopleconnexion PNG application portal.
Open to Port Moresby residents only.
Due to volume of candidates, only short-listed candidates will be contacted regarding applicant progress.
Applications are assessed on merit, capability, and alignment with NCDC’s values and service mandate.
Be part of the team shaping the future of Port Moresby — apply today.

About the Role
The
Technical Officer (Development Engineer)
is a technical support position within the Development Engineering Branch of the Engineering & Infrastructure Division. Based at NCDC City Hall in Waigani, the role operates under the direct supervision of the Civil Engineer and involves working in a high-pressure environment to meet strict deadlines. The position requires proficiency in CAD software and a strong analytical mindset to assist in the review of complex engineering drawings and designs. As a key member of the Planning & Development team, the Technical Officer must maintain high levels of confidentiality, honesty, and professional integrity while supporting the delivery of quality urban infrastructure.
Role Purpose
The primary purpose of the Technical Officer (Development Engineering) is to support the Civil Engineer in the assessment of development applications by collecting and analyzing technical data and measurements. The role focuses on reviewing engineering drawings and plans to ensure they comply with established rules, regulations, and standards for urban development. By providing detailed reports and technical comments, the Technical Officer contributes to a "better design agenda" that ensures the safety, amenity, and functional quality of life for the community in the National Capital District.
Key Responsibilities
Data collection and interpretation – Assist the Civil Engineer to collect, interpret and analysis measurements and design plans, load calculations, and other civil/structural engineering considerations as part of development application review and assessments.
Compliance – ensure that development applications are compliant with all statutory rules, laws, legislations, codes and standards relating to engineering design.
Collaboration and communication within NCDC Planning & Development team – engage and consult with Divisional staff during the examination and review of development submissions to ensure they support NCDC’s goals in achieving a safe, healthy, clean, planned and productive Port Moresby.
Education & Qualifications
Bachelor in Civil Engineering or equivalent from Nationally recognized Institution
Membership with Institution of Engineers PNG Inc./ PNG Institute of Architecture
Additional qualifications in CAD, or other relevant qualifications will be highly desirable
Driver license desirable
Skills & Knowledge
Knowledge in drafting and design
Knowledge of CAD and digital drawing design software
Knowledge of a number of Acts and Regulations including, but not limited to: PNG Building Regulation (1994) (Ch 301), PNG Fire Code, PNG Physical Planning Act (1989), PNG Physical Planning Regulations (1990)
National Capital District Commission Act (2001)
High level computer literacy, including competency in collating and analysing technical information, use and interpretation of CAD software and GIS products.
Experience in the review of detailed and accurate electrical design plans & technical reports.
Excellent report writing skills with ability to self-check and product accurate reports.
Have excellent mathematical, statistical and problem-solving skills, with a highly analytical mindset and attention to detail.
Strong communication and interpersonal skills to collaborate and support staff with fairness, sensitivity, tact, discretion and confidence.
Ability and willingness to work as part of a team and provide a consistently high level of service and output.
Ability to meet demands and deadlines, work under high pressure, maintain confidentiality, be organized, self-disciplined, motivated, honest and reliable.
Must be dedicated to the advancement of NCDC, its goals and vision for Port Moresby
Work Experience
Minimum of one three (3) year experience in a civil engineering capacity
Minimum of one three (3) year experience with using CAD design or relevant software.
